where: PCS capacitor tolerance coverage (earlier: PCM-21, PCM-23; disposition: NEW COVERAGE GAP; independently checked subset stable)
finding: Study Cf +/-5% versus drawn Cf/Cd +/-10% and Rd +/-5%. Independent mixed-corner sweep: 1944/1944 linearly stable. This does not establish all nonlinear/grid modes or all margin rules.
evidence: CODE-VERIFIED; INDEPENDENTLY CALCULATED; ACTUALLY SIMULATED (8 reduced step runs)
recommendation: Read tolerances from the actual assembly; include mixed Cf/Cd/Rd/L/sensor corners in regression tests. Do not describe the gap as proven instability.
closure: A coverage gap, not an instability: the study now reads the assembly tolerances programmatically (Cf, Cd +/-10 %, Rd +/-5 %, L1 / L2, sensor delay) and runs the 1,944-case mixed-corner factorial plus 1,000 random cases: all meet PM >= 40 deg / GM >= 6 dB; worst PM 48.10 deg (SCR 5), worst GM 11.82 dB at a mixed corner (Cd -10 %, Rd +5 %), 0.32 dB below the named corners. Nominal margins identical to the reviewer's independent reproduction (71.15 / 61.38 / 61.68 / 49.04 deg), recorded as corroboration. Side effect: THDu 1.39 / 2.11 % (was 1.31 / 1.98 %), N-leg cascade PM 55 deg / GM 8.2 dB (D-079).

where: PCS gates-off current versus commutation validation (earlier: PCM-07, PCM-21; disposition: OPEN COUPLED PROTECTION PROOF)
finding: Local high threshold 485.5 A plus 3.47 us at 1050 V/120 uH gives 515.9 A, above the 450 A commutation test point and 495 A screening threshold. The source linear overshoot rule gives about 1458 V at a 1048 V bus, above its 1445 V internal design limit; this is a screening estimate, not SPICE or a 1700 V absolute-rating violation.
recommendation: Re-run commutation at the actual gates-off current, joint bus/fault timing, component tolerances and nonlinear inductance; re-coordinate threshold or timing if needed.
closure: Verified with our own leg deck: at the real gates-off current (window top 485.5 A at tolerances + 9.84 A/us on the L1 envelope x the 3.572 us chain = 520.8 A; the reviewer's 515.9 A used a constant 120 uH and the PV channel's 52 ns turn-off) the drawn R_G,off 7.5 ohm peaks at 1457 V against the 1445 V limit (the OV corner 1456 V). Root cause: the gate-resistor sweep ran at the 450 A window nominal and the deck still carried KEMET film values instead of the drawn Jianghai parts. Fix at zero BOM cost: R_G,off 7.5 -> 8.75 ohm (gen/gdrv.py SC40X6): 1437 / 1438 V, admissible current 533.6 A; device loss +16 W, peak efficiency 98.99 -> 98.98 %, turn-off 156 ns inside the 185 ns dead-time minimum. Rejected: 10 ppm/K ladder (-1.8 A of the 15 A needed), faster chain (sensor 2.0 us dominates), +3 films per leg (1444 V only, 4-5 USD, precharge tau over the rating). Published as pcs_spec protection_chain; the control study reads it (D-078).

where: PCS backup path to 600 A (earlier: PCM-21; disposition: OPEN FAULT-INDUCTANCE COVERAGE)
finding: 571.4 A plus 2.86 us at 1050 V requires L >= 105 uH to remain below 600 A. The retrieved construction table ends at 450 A; 107.35 uH held beyond that point gives 599.4 A and is not a guarantee.
recommendation: Specify and validate hot/tolerance incremental L through the complete backup-fault current trajectory, not only through 450 A.
closure: Confirmed: the L1 core cannot hold 105 uH at 600 A hot (-10 % part 87.5 uH at 600 A; +5 % part knee 578 A; flux-rule current 566 A; OpenMagnetics saturation about 553 A), so a backup trip at the drawn 571.4 A band top lets the current run on to about 866 A unless DESAT catches it. A core holding the flux rule to 650 A would cost +32 / +27 USD per three-wire and +43 / +36 USD per four-wire module and would still need a slower turn-off; chosen instead at zero hardware: the CMPSS backup band lowered to top <= 504.2 A / bottom >= 417.3 A (gates off at 533.6 A / 1444.8 V, below every knee), the fault model on the 141-point L1 trajectory (0-700 A, envelope / -10 % / +5 %), the type test 'L(I) to 600 A pulsed at 25 C and with the core at >= 100 C', acceptance at or above the envelope to 566 A. Drawn on PCS-CTL: CMPSS backup DAC +/-1075 codes (0.4285 A per code, DACH 2619 / DACL 469 about the nulled idle zero) = +/-460.7 A, band 423.9-497.5 A at tolerances (6.6 / 6.7 A inside the requirement), gates off at 526.8 A over the 2.964 us backup chain under the 533.6 A ceiling (V_pk about 1441 V, ESTIMATE between deck points); the window / backup overlap rule replaces 'window top < backup bottom' on the PCS variant; the firmware ADC-PPB over-voltage backup lowered 1045 -> 1035 V (band 1019-1051 V) because the bus limit at gates-off is now 1077 V (D-078).

where: PCS grid-forming load steps (earlier: PCM-21; disposition: OPEN NONLINEAR VALIDATION)
finding: New repository averaged model reports 0.380 pu sag on load application and 2.170 pu overshoot on rejection. It omits the diode/DC-link energy-clamp behavior that would change those peaks. Static accuracy and linear stability do not close this event. The separate weak-grid DC-load-rejection case reports recovery at 1098 V, above the actual hardware OV band; a trip-aware recovery model is required.
evidence: REPOSITORY-CLAIM ONLY (reported transient); CODE-VERIFIED model boundaries
recommendation: Simulate actual diode paths, LCL/DC-link energy and current-limited recovery; enforce transient voltage/time limits and validate at the bench. Do not present 2.170 pu as a measured or reliable switched prediction.
closure: A model-boundary gap, closed in the averaged model: the bridge bounded by the modulation limit and the diode clamp, the DC link's finite capacitance absorbing the LCL energy, the 380 A clamp and the hardware OV band in the loop. Firmware adopted: load-current feed-forward (i_L1 - C_eq dv/dt, 1 kHz filter - 2 kHz fails GM at 5.2 dB), an over-voltage deadbeat above 1.2 pu, virtual impedance 0 for a single module. Result at the worst corner: 0.43 / 1.77 pu (was 0.38 / 2.17 pu unbounded, now labelled superseded), within 10 % after <= 3.4 ms and 1 % after <= 25 ms; declared envelope <= 1.9 pu to 0.5 ms, <= 1.3 pu to 3 ms, <= 1.1 pu to 20 ms and >= 0.35 / 0.75 / 0.88 pu (ITIC-style class FROM MEMORY; IEC 62040-3 class 1 not claimed). Weak-grid DC-load rejection trip-aware: the loop alone 1,098 V; with the protection the gates go off at 1,001-1,068 V and the bus is left at 1,094-1,106 V latched; on a battery-less bus a DC/DC must cut its current within 0.51 ms (PV firmware row), else the bus ends at 1,048-1,117 V above the aux's 1,107 V lock-out; weak-grid CV-mode power limits 89.5 kW at SCR 5 / 119.5 kW at SCR 10 / full from SCR 20; the soft-OV row holds the DC loop in CV mode. Bench and a switched model remain the gate (D-079).

where: PCS full-power stiff-grid LVRT (earlier: PCM-05, PCM-21; disposition: OPERATING RESTRICTION)
finding: Reported onset current 484/465/445 A at 0/0.1/0.2 pu residual grid voltage can cross the 426 A low trip edge. Published pre-fault limits 95.5/105.5/115 kW are not full 125 kW ride-through.
recommendation: Apply pre-fault derating where required or redesign/revalidate onset protection and control. Confirm applicable grid-code requirements from actual standard/connection text.
closure: Same onset currents verified (484 / 465 / 445 A). A cheaper firmware measure removes the pre-fault restriction: in the ride-through state the per-sample clamp drops to 270 A and predicts on the C_f voltage with the divider's pole inverted - onset 382 A, 403 A at the worst corner and dip instant (23 A margin to the 426 A window edge); D-077's statement that no firmware can catch the onset is withdrawn. The derating stays as the stated fallback: rated current passes up to SCR 83.9 / 119.9 / 198.3 at 0 / 0.1 / 0.2 pu; derating engages at an estimated SCR >= 64.5 (0.2 pu reactive-current step estimator, accuracy ASSUMED +/-30 %); installation declaration 8.07 MVA fault level per 125 kW module. The reactive-current injection profile and the connection-code figures stay FROM MEMORY with the standard text as the gate; the 23 A margin needs the bench and a switched model (D-079).

where: AC-start and transfer state machine (earlier: PCM-21; disposition: NEW STATE COVERAGE GAP)
finding: New grid tap and AC precharge are drawn, but the control report explicitly excludes AC startup as a state of its checked machine.
evidence: CODE-VERIFIED hardware source; REPOSITORY-CLAIM ONLY state coverage
recommendation: Include AC start, source loss, welded/stuck relay, undervoltage, retries and transition-to-rectifier in an executable fault-injected state machine.
closure: The executable fault-injected state machine now contains the AC start: 17 states, all invariants hold, 35 fault cases (source loss, welded / stuck relay and contactor, brown-out, timeouts, retries, transition to rectifier mode). Five holes in the sequence as specified were found and repaired: H1 relay test only on a precharged link (on a dead link a welded contactor made it an unprecharged close); H2 the welded check as a voltage-difference test valid on a charged link (the 50 V check could never pass on a retry); H3 the closing permissive re-checked within 20 ms of the close (a sagging grid closed onto a drained link); H4 no K_PRE -> K_B route onto a battery below the grid peak (rectifier mode first); H5 the attempt counter in the recorder flash (RAM counters reset on brown-out); plus an own AC-start stop state (CONTROLLED STOP would have closed the DC contactor). Carried into the pcs_spec hand-over and the control-board firmware table (D-079).
